#6817. How to Maintain Long, Healthy Hair Over 50, According to Experts

From top treatments to when to plan your next trim, here’s everything to know

Every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

There’s something undeniably chic about a head of long, luscious hair. Think glossy, waist-skimming, bouncy, voluminous lengths that make extensions an option rather than a long-term commitment. What’s more, long hair provides the ultimate canvas for experimentation, with styling possibilities that feel limitless.

As hair matures, however, maintaining the same level of shine, strength, and vitality can require more attention. As texture changes and dryness increases, the key is to adapt your routine to give your longer lengths the care they deserve. “Long hair can look beautiful at any age, but keeping mature hair glossy and healthy-looking is all about replenishing moisture and maintaining shine,” says celebrity hairstylist Naomi Brooks. “I always recommend prioritising hydrating products that help smooth the hair cuticle, improve softness, and enhance shine, alongside regular trims to keep the lengths and ends looking healthy.”

If you’re considering making the transition and letting your bob grow out, look to a host of celebrities for inspiration. From Demi Moore and Naomi Campbell to Andie MacDowell and Claudia Schiffer, countless iterations are proving just how effortless long hair can look on women over 50. As Brooks explains: “Demi Moore is a fantastic example of how beautiful long hair can look at any age. Her hair is consistently glossy, healthy-looking, and full of movement.”

While genetics certainly play a role, Moore’s glossy lengths are also the result of great care and strategic products. Her hairstylist, Dimitris Giannetos, revealed on social media that he often relies on Kérastase’s Gloss Absolu Glaze Drops Anti-Frizz Hair Oil to reduce frizz, boost shine, and ensure hair remains sleek without looking too heavy. Indeed, experts recommend investing in a high-quality hydrating treatment to ensure mature hair is treated with extra care. “Mature hair can become drier, finer or more fragile over time, so maintaining moisture and shine is important,” says Warren Edwards, creative director at Warren & the Hare.

Additionally, for those with gray or silver hair, session stylist Danilo Giangreco recommends incorporating a clear gloss into your routine to enhance shine. This can also help counteract any unwanted brassiness, ensuring hair appears brighter and healthier.

Another expert-approved tip is to keep heat styling to a minimum where possible. If you do rely on hot tools, applying heat protectant can help shield strands from damage while preserving moisture, strength, and shine.

Finally, contrary to popular belief, long hair thrives on regular maintenance. Though it may seem counterintuitive when trying to grow your hair, routine appointments are essential to keep split ends at bay and prevent the ends from looking too thin or tired. In turn, this helps keep long, mature hair looking fuller, healthier, and overall more glossy.

#6816. The Fall Essentials You Need According to 4 of the Most Stylish Guys We Know

Grails, staples, and everyday beaters abound.

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

Fall has the singular ability to turn even the most Spartan man into a bit of a style savant. It’s like a wolf awakens the second that temperatures start to drop. Suddenly you see an Instagram post from the junior analyst below you; he must fancy himself a budding A$AP Rocky, because he’s rocking a statement scarf. Your brother-in-law is wearing a turtleneck. Your buddy is in white jeans. Every day, you zone out in dumb stakeholder meetings and fantasize about a new jacket or that pair of buttery-soft leather loafers you saw on a dude at the grocery store.

It’s because fall invites more—more layers, more textures. It can be freeing. No more worrying if that T-shirt will become a body scan of where and how you sweat; no more worrying if those pants will suffocate you. But ... it can be too much. How should you layer? How can you get funky for the holiday party without looking like an asshole? What brands are even worth buying?

We answer all those questions elsewhere in this magazine, but today we want you to take a breath. Keep it simple. How? By following some good examples.

A lot of the best-dressed guys right now are trimming down their wardrobes in favor of focusing on the basics. “This fall I’ve tried to trim the fat and make do with a much smaller wardrobe,” says actor, content creator, and friend of the magazine Albert Muzquiz—better known online by his handle @edgyalbert. “I only have a few shirts, a few pants, and a couple jackets—and I feel like I’m dressing better than ever.”

So instead of lobbing a bunch of meaningless trends, or -cores, at you, we decided to send you to some of the best-dressed men of the moment. You’ve heard enough from us; here’s what they’re feeling this fall.

Jake Mueser, founder of the eponymous bespoke suiting brand J. Mueser, has a handful of fall essentials. That cohort includes a cream turtleneck, which “you can throw on with anything,” as well as a classic tweed or herringbone blazer—same idea. They’re easy but plenty damn sexy.

Mueser also extols the virtues of a classic flannel suit—perhaps like the one he makes. “It works with everything from a denim shirt to a tie,” he says. “I like to break it up, wearing the jacket with vintage light-wash Wrangler cowboy cuts.” (A move we wholeheartedly endorse.)

J. Mueser Waverly Herringbone Virgin Wool-Tweed Blazer

J. Mueser Ivory Chunky Merino Roll-Neck Sweater

J. Mueser Charcoal Churchill Stripe Flannel Waverly Suit

There are a few reasons Drew Thomas can’t stop recommending merino sweaters—the thin, almost jersey sort—to his more than 500,000 TikTok followers. “You can get so much wear out of one,” he says. “You can layer it in the fall, wear it on its own on a slightly warmer day, or tie it around your shoulders. It works in the spring too, and even on a summer night when it gets a little cooler.”

Another seasonally versatile piece Thomas will stand ten toes down for is cream pants. In fact, Thomas likes to wear his all through fall. He keeps a few pairs on constant rotation. “I feel like the cream breaks up those darker fall colors and lets them stand out more,” he says.

When it comes to his next fall investment, Thomas is taking cues from the British sartorial invasion (“It never really went away, but it definitely feels like it’s having a moment again”) and looking to Barbour. “Something timeless and practical that I can wear for years and that only gets better with age,” he says. “I love the idea of owning something that develops character over time and could eventually be passed down to someone else. Those are the kinds of pieces I feel are worth investing in.”

J. Crew Relaxed-Fit Double-Pleated Corduroy Pant

“A down vest is my favorite fall garment,” Esquire contributor Christopher Fenimore told us. “It’s an easy outerwear piece to layer stuff under. I run hot, and I like having parts of my body exposed to the elements.”

We second that, but more predictably he highlights the entire category of shirting. Jackets and layers get a lot of shine, but this is the layer that, no matter how much temperatures fluctuate, will be on the skin. It’s a great time to get a few good oxford-cloth button-downs, polos, or beefier tees.

This time of year is also a great time to get clinical. “I assess things I have that might need updates, in terms of fit and silhouette or different fabrications depending on how I’d wear them,” he says. That can be rebuying your preferred undershirt or socks, or it could be a good time to jump on that thinner, more versatile merino sweater wave.

“Fall is the best time to break in a new pair of denim,” Muzquiz says. Wear it hard enough now and “it’ll be soft enough and possibly breathable enough for wear during the spring and parts of the summer.” No better time to get something esoteric.

When it comes to fall shoes, Muzquiz is into a classic six-inch lace-up boot. “There are so many bullshit brands out there that are trying to fool you with budget options,” he says. “Just get a pair of Red Wing Heritage if you’re starting out or Viberg if you really wanna flex.”

Muzquiz also finds himself taking part in the “buttery, delicate loafer movement” that’s been picking up steam as of late. The Yardee Moccasin loafers from Vinny’s are his pick of the bunch.

#6813. Luke Grimes Didn’t Know If Marshals Would Work Without Kayce’s Wife

“He wants his little slice of heaven,” Grimes told Esquire when Yellowstone ended. “It’s that simple.”

Coming back home isn’t easy, especially for Luke Grimes. The Yellowstone actor spent all of the hit Taylor Sheridan drama as Kayce Dutton, a man trying to leave the past behind and move on from the sins of his father, family patriarch John Dutton (Kevin Costner). But when the western ended and Grimes had to say goodbye to the cast, crew, and his onscreen wife Kelsey Asbille (who played Monica Dutton), he really thought it was for the last time.

“Hopefully everyone can see that it was time,” Grimes told Esquire when Yellowstone ended. “There’s always talks of spin-offs. I’d do it [but] I just don’t understand how it would work once the story ends. Kayce wants to cowboy and be happy with his family. He doesn’t want to kill people anymore. He doesn’t want the weight of a huge mega ranch that isn’t sustainable in today’s times. He wants his little slice of heaven. It’s that simple.”

Paramount offered Grimes the option to return anyway on Marshals, a spin-off of Yellowstone that sees Kayce Dutton join the U.S. Marshals service in Montana. Reportedly, they won him over after pitching that they would take everything from Kayce so that he would be forced to start again. First on the chopping block? His wife, Monica.

“The thing I was most worried about doing Marshals was doing it without Kelsey,” Grimes told ScreenRant during an interview for season 2 last week. “I just couldn’t wrap my head around Kayce without Monica. That was the story. The rest of Yellowstone was about people fighting over land, and I just loved my wife. I had my own thing going on, and so I didn’t know what that would even look like.”

Eventually he came around to the idea. “Once I sort of, you know, could wrap my head around the fact that that was going to open up all these new storylines,” he admitted, “we just [had] to make sure we do honor [their life together] and don’t try to skip over it or pretend it didn’t happen.”

Marshals season 2 continues to air this fall, as Kayce Dutton explores a potential new relationship with fellow Marshal Andrea Cruz (Ash Santos). Sometime this season, former Yellowstone fan favorite Jimmy (Jefferson White) will also make an appearance.

The old Taylor can’t come to the phone right now

Over the years, Taylor Swift has changed her hair often, switched up her style, and gone through many eras, but one constant has been her iconic red lip. Swift has worn the notable blue-red color for decades—through multiple tours, relationships, and possibly even at her wedding—but more recently, she’s branched out and ditched her signature red for something a bit juicier.

On Monday, the Recording Academy announced the 2027 Grammy nominations, and Swift made a surprise appearance on the livestream to announce two of the categories, “Album of the Year” and “Song of the Year,” but her appearance wasn’t the only surprise. Instead of her classic red lip, Swift wore “cinnamon latte lips”—a burnt-orange shade that may be our favorite hue for the fall season. One might assume “cinnamon latte lips” would skew more brown, but the way Swift wears it, the color has a bit of orange. The lipstick shade also resembles the one Swift wore when announcing her recent single “Patient Zero” back in September.

Although Swift swapped her red for a warm brown-orange hue for the Grammys announcement, she still wore her classic winged eyeliner and bangs—two other staples of her beauty look. This isn’t the first time she’s shaken up her lip look. More recently, Swift has leaned more neutral, with a petal-pink lip at the sixth annual Academy Museum Gala and the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards. But she’s not completely forgoing her red lip, as it still seems to be a staple look, especially at her husband Travis Kelce’s Kansas City Chiefs games.

Swift hasn’t explicitly shared what lipstick she is wearing in the video. However, her makeup artist, Lorrie Turk, has previously confirmed that she often wears the Nars lipstick in Morocco, a warm, neutral cinnamon shade with an orange undertone, so she may have worn the same shade during the Grammys announcements.

#6810. The Best LED Mirrors for Your Bathroom

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

It might sound dumb, but a smart option can improve your routine.

What is an LED mirror, and do you need one? These mirrors use an illuminated strip of light that you control to give more measured, even lighting than your bathroom overhead can. Some have a front light strip, some have backlighting, others have both. The best are equipped with antifog tech to make sure your mirror stays clear and functional during your entire post-shower routine. You’ll appreciate that when you’re shaving, and your wife won’t be able to go back to applying makeup without it. Because they use LEDs, they don’t use a significant amount of energy, and—so far—they are still low-tech enough to be largely free of AI.

So if they are so great, why doesn’t everyone have one of these fancy mirrors? The truth is it’s still hard to find a good one. The interest is there, but the market is currently flooded with $100 mirrors on Amazon that will work for a handful of months and then crap out on you. And the real good ones—the ones that merge tech and design—are expensive. These four run the gamut from affordable and convenient to luxe, but they all have one thing in common: You won’t be sending them back.

Everyone starts somewhere. And honestly the $200 Amazon option isn’t a terrible place to begin—it’s got over 3,000 reviews that mostly agree with me. Really this is everything that comes standard in a smart LED mirror: touch-controlled light settings, a defogging mode, and multiple power options (with a wall-plug option for apartments and more temporary dwellings).

The only real problem I can see is the design. The thick LED strip takes up a considerable amount of mirror real estate. Other, more thoughtful designs forgo this issue with thinner strips or backlighting. To be fair, you can turn that light off and just run with the backlight, but the chunky design of the mirror’s frame still shows.

If you want to just browse LED mirrors, Visual Comfort has a wide range of designer lighted mirrors. This one is not quite as striking, clearly, as the $2,000 options, but for $400 this is a trustworthy smart mirror that will have just what you want. What I especially like about the Mera is that you can separately adjust the brightness and color temperature.

For something really high-quality on all fronts, you’re going to have to pay top dollar. This is part of Visual Comfort’s Signature Collection, by designer Thomas O’Brien. What that really says is, from a design and craftsmanship angle, this is going to be a great mirror first—one that will last. Unfortunately, that does mean some of the tech comes secondary and not always in a way you might want.

But first off, the look. The gorgeous iron frame has a gilded finish that gives it a gold sheen. If you have the money to shell out for something fancier, this mirror is offered in nickel or (for the real high rollers) brass.

While it looks nice and has three brightness and color-temperature settings you can toggle between, it lacks any other “smart” features. Namely, there’s no defogging mode. And if you want this one installed, you’ll need to have an electrician do it.

The real problem with 99 percent of these mirrors is they just don’t look as natural or clean in your bathroom as a regular-ass mirror. This one from Seura actually does. When the backlight is not on, nobody will be able to tell the difference. When it is, you’ll reap all the benefits of a light that you can control.

These mirrors are a made-to-order, assembled-in-the-U.S.A. (Wisconsin, to be precise) type of deal. You can get them in all kinds of dimensions and, yes, even in a round shape, if that’s what you’re looking for. For dimming, you can have a control switch installed on the wall alongside the mirror or get the version that has touch controls.

#6809. 11 Winter Colognes You Can Get for Under $100

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

Smelling great doesn’t have to cost a fortune.

There’s never been a better time to get into personal fragrance. The cologne market is booming with frequent new launches from luxury fashion houses and perfumeries, yes—but it’s also filled with tons of great scents from more accessible and affordable brands. And with the temperatures finally dropping below 50°F in New York and Thanksgiving coming up next week, we’re officially in winter mode. That means getting our puffer coats out of storage and changing up our seasonal fragrance rotation.

So out with the fresh, aquatic, citrusy fragrances that belong on the beach and in with the warm, spicy, smoky scents that make the wintertime feel cozy. We’re talking cardamom and cloves, smoky tobacco and incense, sweet vanilla and smooth amber. Want to capture the scent of sitting by the fireplace and sipping a hot cocoa while wearing a cashmere sweater? These scents will do that—and at a fraction of the cost of a designer fragrance. We rounded up our picks for the winter that all come in at under $100, so you can save the big bucks for holiday shopping.

If you’ve checked out any of our other affordable-cologne roundups, you won’t be surprised to see Cremo at the top of our list here. We talk about the brand a lot, but it’s for a good reason: Cremo’s colognes are some of our favorites out there, and they literally cost under $25 each. Spice & Black Vanilla is our favorite spicy scent from the lineup, and the warm blend of cardamom, vanilla, tobacco, and woods is perfect for winter. Wear it for a cold-weather date night, a fancy dinner, or really any occasion.

Want a decent cologne mist you can easily buy on Amazon for just $13? Old Spice has been around for almost 90 years—yes, it may remind you of your dad, but it’s been around for so long because it’s a classic that just works. But shaking things up a bit, the brand released a new collection of cologne mists earlier this year, which includes this Cashmere & Vanilla Wood scent bursting with spices and powdery iris. For $13, you might as well order a few.

One of our favorite boozy colognes (and all-time favorite colognes in general) is Jazz Club from Maison Margiela’s Replica line. It’s one you’ve probably heard of and read about many times in our fragrance roundups, and since the 1 oz bottle is only $89, I just couldn’t leave it off this list. With rum, tobacco, and vanilla bean at the center, Jazz Club is the olfactory equivalent of sipping a cocktail in a smoke-filled bar. In other words, it’s the perfect sexy winter scent.

Gap recently introduced a new addition to its revitalized fragrance line (originally from the ’90s): Bliss. The gourmand EDP adds some creamy sweetness to the otherwise mostly fresh and earthy collection, and it came just in time for winter. It delights the senses with notes of butterscotch, cocoa bean, coconut milk, and vanilla bourbon, and it’s practically making my mouth water just thinking about it.

Huron has only five different scents, but it’s a true example of a brand that puts quality over quantity. I love each and every one of the brand’s EDPs, and while the marine Sea Salt + Driftwood and Original Citrus + Eucalyptus are both fresh and perfect for the summer, the Sandalwood + Black Pepper fragrance is definitely our winter choice. It’s warm, woody, and spicy, with some airy florals at the heart and rich amber and more woods at the base.

If you like the scent of Tom Ford’s Oud Wood but can’t get past that $300 price tag, we hear you. That’s why House of Twist made Wood No. 28; it’s not exactly Oud Wood, but it’s close enough. And for just $48, we’ll take it. The fragrance is a nice blend of nutty cardamom, oud wood, vanilla, and creamy sandalwood—a combination pretty much anyone can get behind.

Making the cut at $99 is Phlur’s newest fragrance: Heavy Cream. It’s a rich gourmand that’s balanced out by some bright citrus and airy florals at the top and heart of the fragrance, so it doesn’t get too overwhelmingly heavy. It definitely has the notes you’d expect of a fragrance inspired by heavy cream, like vanilla, amber, and creamy musks.

Fine’ry is another one of our go-to brands when it comes to affordable colognes we actually like. And this winter, our top choice from the lineup is Smoke & Leather, which smells like—you guessed it—smoky tobacco and rich leather with some woody undertones. It definitely brings the heat on a cold day.

Boy Smells is known for pairing traditionally masculine and feminine scent notes for truly unisex fragrances that anyone can enjoy. Hinoki Fantôme is a fan favorite thanks to its blend of spices, woods, and smoke, which are underscored by earthy oakmoss, orris, and patchouli. You really can’t put this fragrance in one category, because it spans so many. It’s a complex fragrance that really works, especially for the winter.

Earthy scents are chameleons that can work in any season, so it really just matters what they’re paired with. In the instance of Stetson’s Free Rein from its new Untamed collection, the pairing of earthy notes of wild verbena, sweetgrass, prairie moss, and patchouli with vetiver smoke and red amber makes it a warm, rich fragrance that adds some heat to your cold-weather outfit.

Florals are, generally speaking, made for spring and summer—but sometimes you get a gorgeous blend of florals with woods, musks, or amber, and it becomes perfect for wintertime. That’s exactly what Lafco has done with its Golden Morning scent: It’s got light floral notes of apple blossom, lavender, violet leaf, and rose, which all play nicely with a rich, sweet base of woods, honey, amber, and musks.

We found the stuff they don’t already own.

This is not meant to sound like a brag, but it inevitably will. Tons of luxurious products come across our desks; as such, I’ve developed especially discerning taste. I’ve tested more than my fair share of $500 colognes, $700 headphones, and $1,000 espresso machines over the years. Not that luxury is synonymous with price, but you know. While these occupational hazards might make me a challenge to shop for, they also give me a discerning eye for gifts that will actually impress my fellow snobs.

If they’re a coffee connoisseur who only drinks single-origin, always espresso, consider upgrading their at-home setup with Meraki’s dual-boiler espresso machine. For the audiophile whose vinyl collection rivals that of an actual record store, a Fluance turntable will do their records justice. And if their vanity would put a Saks to shame, an under-the-radar Creed fragrance and an award-winning red light mask are worthy additions.

The last thing they want is a bad interface or those ugly Alexa models. Thankfully, 2026 is the year Apple entered the home display market.

My brother has the most extensive at-home espresso setup I’ve ever seen, and he swears by this tamper. It’s spring-loaded to deliver consistent pressure, with an integrated lever for perfectly even pucks. If your espresso pulls aren’t flawless after this, time to look inward.

For a gift that will impress even the most particular of coffee connoisseurs, go with Meraki’s second-gen espresso machine. Featuring a built-in grinder, scales, and a dual-boiler system, it’s one of the most premium machines money can buy.

The ultimate snob’s wine opener. A needle and a bit of fancy pump work allow you to pour a glass without ever uncorking the bottle. Great for by-the-glass or sparing yourself any cork emergencies with older vintages.

Take it from someone who actually cooks—the home chef in your life doesn’t want gimmicky gadgets. Instead, gift them practical, high-quality cookware they’ll actually use, like this editor favorite stainless steel frying pan from All-Clad’s D3 line.

For the foodie who worships at the altar of Bourdain, consider gifting them his exact chef’s knife of choice. The Japanese-made Global G-2 has sleek all-metal construction, with a textured handle for a nonslip grip. What’s more, it can be custom-engraved with their name or initials.

For the giftee who’s always complaining that their matcha isn’t the right color (guilty), consider this tea kit. It has everything they need for the perfect cup at home, including a sifter, measuring spoon, whisk, and ceremonial-grade matcha.

Dubbed our top pick for audiophiles, this turntable has it all: consistently great audio quality, a built-in speed control mechanism, and an attractive wood finish.

Aesthetics and audio quality don’t always go hand-in-hand for headphones, which is precisely why this Bang & Olufsen pair is a standout. Our editors named it the best pair of noise-canceling headphones for sound quality, and it’s easily the most attractive model on the list.

If they’ve ever slept at one of the world’s best hotels, they have slept on Frette sheets and worn a Frette robe. Give them that luxury at home.

Every chess player I’ve ever met takes the game extremely seriously, and this is a set they’d be proud to display on their coffee table. Bonus: You can monogram it for a personal touch.

The best home gifts not only spark conversation, but also serve a purpose in their space. Pair this Greek mythology-inspired incense holder with some great-smelling incense (I’m partial to Le Labo), and you have an infallible gift for the artsy types on your list.

All the interior design obsessives I know in Brooklyn (myself included) are obsessed with this lighting brand, which draws from Bauhaus and mid-century modern influences. This retro, saucer-shaped table lamp is a foolproof pick for the giftee who wouldn’t be caught dead turning on “the big light.”

I have to hand it to the cinephiles here: Dolby Atmos is truly superior for watching movies (sorry, films) at home. This Sonos soundbar offers unmatched 3D surround-sound in a sleek package.

A candle is only “impersonal” if it’s ugly or smells bad. Loewe’s incense candle is beautiful, and it smells divine. No snob will ever turn one down.

Sure, Aventus might be Creed’s most popular cologne, but the fragrance snob you know doesn’t want to smell like every other guy. Instead, opt for one of the brand’s under-the-radar scents, like Bois du Portugal. Its notes of lavender, sandalwood, and cedar offer an aromatic scent reminiscent of a vintage barbershop.

Ah, the status hand soap. A gift that works for virtually anyone, especially those with discerning taste. This pick from Nécessaire somehow feels less sceney than other options on the market, and it’s infused with skin-softening ingredients like vitamin B3 and linoleic acid.

As a fragrance expert who tests new scents for a living, few earn me as many compliments as Althair from Parfums de Marly. It’s a grown-up vanilla, with notes of orange blossom, cinnamon, and a dose of smoky guaiac wood to keep it from going saccharine. Although it’s technically from the men’s line, its not-too-sweet gourmand scent profile is truly genderless.

The iRestore red light face mask just won a 2026 Gadget Award. Enough said.

Their parched, damaged strands deserve nothing but the best; in this case, it’s Kérastase’s Oléo-Relax hair mask. It’s got a ton of hydrating ingredients—rose oil, coconut oil, and shorea oil—to replenish dry hair. Not to mention, it smells damn good.

#6802. How to Reset Your Skin Care Routine After 40

Dermatologists break down the ingredients, steps, and treatments that matter most for skin over 40.

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

As we age, there’s seemingly always something new to think about, including adjusting your skin care routine to meet your skin’s evolving needs. You may not need to add a bunch of new products to your current regimen, but increased dryness, changes in texture, fine lines, and enlarged pores may require ingredient swaps that your current lineup can’t deliver. The skin care products you used in your 20s and 30s may have worked then, but once you hit 40, your skin may start to need something different. Experts share how to reset your routine for 40+ skin, including the non-negotiables, new ingredients that can have the greatest impact, and what to avoid to keep your maturing skin looking and feeling its best.

Over 40, skin has already started to thin, at both the epidermis and dermis levels, explains Dr. Suzan Obagi, a board-certified dermatologist, associate professor of dermatology and plastic surgery, and director of the UPMC Cosmetic Surgery & Skin Health Center. “This means that skin will start to appear more fragile, fine lines will start to show, and skin becomes drier. For these reasons, a good skin care regimen should include a retinoid (retinol, retinaldehyde, or tretinoin) to help improve skin thickness, increase extracellular matrix proteins (collagen, elastin, and glycosaminoglycans (GAGs)), and encourage fibroblasts to make more of our Natural Moisturizing Factor (NMF),” Obagi tells ELLE.

Most skin over 40 also has some sun damage, which Obagi says can present as freckles and sun spots. Well before 40 and certainly after, there’s one daily non-negotiable for skin of any age: sunscreen. If the spots have already shown up, Obagi recommends a skin-brightening serum with tranexamic acid (TXA), antioxidants, and peptides to help correct the hyperpigmentation.

Additionally, Dr. Chris Tomassian, a California-based, board-certified dermatologist and founder of The Dermatology Collective, says a retinol at night will go a long way, as will vitamin C in the morning and aggressive moisturization.

As for ingredients, Tomassian says the key players in the post-40 reset will be retinol, SPF, and vitamin C, as already noted, along with PDRN, ectoin, ceramides, and occasionally estradiol.

If you’re not already on a daytime and nighttime routine, now’s the time to start.

Morning: Use a gentle cleanser if your skin is oily or if you didn’t get to a proper wash the night before. Tomassian suggests skipping the cleanse if your skin feels dry when you wake up. Follow with a good antioxidant like an L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) serum or one with tetrahexyldecyl ascorbate (THD), silymarin, or phloretin. Layer on a PDRN moisturizer and SPF before any makeup.

Night: Before bed, cleanse thoroughly to remove makeup and sunscreen. Layer on a copper peptide serum, ptiox treatment, tretinoin (retinol), and a PDRN moisturizer. Obagi also suggests combining a pigment-correcting serum with a retinoid to help build the dermis extracellular matrix and target hyperpigmentation.

Bonus steps: Exfoliate one to two times each week with a combination peel pad, alpha hydroxy or beta hydroxy acids depending on your skin’s dryness level or if you’re experiencing any breakout. Tomassian warns, though, that post-40 skin should avoid over-exfoliating. “Skin gets drier with age, and breaking down your skin barrier by scrubbing or peeling too aggressively or too often can leave skin vulnerable to drying out,” he explains.

At any age, consistency is key. Even if you’re lucky enough to have minimal signs of aging, both experts agree that these steps will go a long way. “It is still important to incorporate a retinoid, an antioxidant, and a good moisturizer into your daily routine,” says Obagi.

There’s plenty you can do at home to care for your skin after 40, including adding LED light therapy to your lineup to help with fine lines and wrinkles and stimulate collagen—but Tomassian notes these are only beneficial if you use them consistently. An even greater investment is pairing your home routine with regular visits to a professional for in-office procedures like microneedling or ablative and nonablative lasers. These treatments can jump-start your skin to start producing more collagen. For chronic sun damage like redness and dark spots, Tomassian recommends Intense Pulsed Light (IPL), Picosure, or DermaV/Fraxel/CO2 lasers. These devices target pigmentation concerns that skin care does little to improve.

Obagi adds that pro visits are important since collagen production peaks at age 18 and, with each passing year, our skin makes 1 percent less collagen, elastin, and GAGs. “By our mid-30s and early 40s, we would benefit from devices that boost collagen production periodically. These can be noninvasive lasers, microneedling, and radiofrequency devices. These will boost collagen for a short time, but when combined with a well-thought-out skin care regimen, the results can be prolonged,” says Obagi.

You’ve lived with your skin for 40+ years, so you can tell when things start to change. Obagi says you have to listen to your own skin. “If you are on the dry side or have fragile skin, avoid harsh ingredients such as glycolic or lactic acid, strong retinoids, or over-exfoliating with scrubs. These can irritate the skin and drive sensitivity,” she highlights. If you have thicker skin or are oilier, she suggests exfoliating fruit acids and says your skin can tolerate stronger retinoids.

Tomassian’s rule of thumb is that after age 30, use as many ingredients as possible to bank collagen and focus on thicker moisturizers as you get older, since we produce less oil.

Key ingredients: oat-derived surfactants, plant-derived humectants, polyhydroxy acids

Key ingredients: liposomal tranexamic acid (TXA), oligopeptide-68, THD, and hydrolyzed algin to help target the various pathways driving pigmentation

Key ingredients: stabilized vitamin C, hyaluronic acid, panthenol, soothing allantoin, and green tea extract

Key ingredients: collagen, copper peptides, smoothing and brightening niacinamide, retinal, rice PDRN

Key ingredients: low-molecular PDRN, moisturizing squalane, panthenol, and ceramide, brightening niacinamide, firming rose peptide

Key ingredients: glycolic acid, lactic acid, malic acid, antioxidant-rich resveratrol, and green tea extract

Key ingredients: 10 percent Homosalate, 5 percent Octisalate, 3 percent Avobenzone, brightening niacinamide and ethyl ascorbic acid; moisturizing argan oil, squalane, and bisabolol

#6799. The Masculinity Defenders Are Already Whining About Robert Pattinson’s James Bond

Every incel with a YouTube account thinks R-Patz isn’t manly enough to be the face of a film franchise that contains a movie called Octopussy.

After an exhaustive and exhausting years-long casting process, Robert Pattinson has been announced as the new James Bond, and right on cue, the masculinity defenders are being super normal about it.

I thought the big takeaway was that we have the first James Bond with a cute little social media nickname (which led me to wonder whether we’d have been calling Pierce Brosnan “P-Broz” if there had been a Twitter in 1995). But nope: the deal is that R-Patz is not manly enough to be the face of a film franchise that contains a movie called Octopussy.

On a YouTube show called Dan Wootton: Outspoken, special guest and self-described “right-wing comedian” Leo Kearse said Pattinson is “Not a man! He doesn’t have a hairy chest, no drink problem, he’s never bought a fridge.” Okay! Point by point: 1) Daniel Craig was smooth as a baby seal. 2) Watch The Lighthouse if you think R-Patz can’t convincingly put them away. 3) What?

Kearse, ignorant and undeterred as a real man ought to be, continues: “He probably still sleeps in a car shaped like a Ferrari, with Powerpuff Girls sheets.” Also he and Wootton both seem to be calling him “Robert Patterson” throughout. Great stuff. I mean this, Leo Kearse: you are the funniest right-wing comedian I’ve ever seen.

Interesting, except that the next Bond movie will be written by British screenwriter Steven Knight, who wrote the ultra-violent Eastern Promises, created the epic gangster series Peaky Blinders, and co-created Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, which doesn’t have anything to do with James Bond or the broader masculinity conversation per se, but goddamn what a career.

In The Atlantic, Tom Nichols complained that “Pattinson lacks the manly gravitas …Pattinson is sensitive; he broods; he’s conflicted.” He concludes, “I imagine that when the mad criminal offers him a mint julep, Pattinson will scowl and explain that alcohol and sugar are bad for you.” Listen: if there’s anything more masculine than imagining a scenario and then getting angry at it, it’s fretting endlessly about what is and is not masculine.

Right under a piece whining that “the left-wing bias of The Grammys is on full display” (because Michelle Obama got a Best Audiobook nomination and Jesse Welles’s “No Kings” is nominated for Best Americana Roots Recording), the Blaze wrote a pretty straightforward news post about the casting, and although it’s journalistic malpractice to quote any comments section to prove any larger societal point, when you get comments like…

“Is he still licensed to kill, or will he be an unarmed social worker with a handbook on de-escalation negotiation?”

On social media and comments sections and whatever that Dan Wootton show is, exhibit A for the case against Robert Pattinson’s masculinity is a 2023 Paris Fashion Week red carpet look: Pattinson in a fur jacket and a skirt. I don’t know, I think a man ought to defy conventions, go his own way, take some risks. Plus, the dude can rock a skirt. Don’t hate him because he’s beautiful.

So Pattinson is too fey to play Bond, and too famous from other iconic roles besides. This is, of course, the exact criticism leveled at Roger Moore in 1972 when he took the role over: that he was too lithe to compete with the hairy-shouldered thickness of Sean Connery, and that he was already too well-known for having played a similar role in The Saint. (And for having done it on television; “TV Star” was an epithet until right around The Sopranos.) Timothy Dalton was dinged for being too Shakespearean to take over for Moore. Pierce Brosnan had already played a parody of a Bond type on Remington Steele, so how could he compete with the gravitas of Dalton? Daniel Craig was criticized for being too beefy to take over for Brosnan. You can’t win.

The good news is that as much whining as there is about Pattinson and his lack of masculinity, there’s a lot less of it than there would have been even a few months ago. The “not man enough” chorus is singing, but they’re undeniably a little bit muted. Whether it has anything to do with Pete Hegseth and Markwayne Mullin and Sean Duffy and the rest of our government’s drag king grotesques of manliness publicly tripping on their dicks and compromising our basic security in the process I can’t say definitively, but it sure feels like it.

Among the many YouTube reaction videos, I came upon one that I am absolutely not going to watch, but whose title distills the argument down to its essence almost too perfectly.

There it is. I wanted someone else. The new thing is bad. The whole argument, like so many of the arguments against the evolution of masculinity, boils down to “things aren’t the way they were when I was younger, and I’m angry about it.” It’s the credo of the dull, the philosophy of the frightened, the logline of at least three Tim Allen sitcoms. Move on. Grow up. Let R-Patz cook.

I’ll meet you back here when we’re furious about Taylor Swift doing the theme song.

#6795. How to Watch Every Movie in the Marvel Cinematic Universe

It’s easy. You only need time. And a Disney+ subscription.

Suddenly, we’re excited about Marvel again. Hitting theaters on December 18 is Avengers: Doomsday, the long-awaited next Avengers sequel. You may have heard that Robert Downey Jr. is back, only now in the role of the villainous Doctor Doom instead of Iron Man. As the man himself said back at San Diego Comic-Con in July 2024: “New mask, same task.” Whatever that means. (Also, if you think you ever heard of something called Avengers: The Kang Dynasty, no, you didn’t.)

Anyway, it’s been seven years since we last saw a new Avengers movie. Back then, you might have Googled something like, “How to watch every Marvel movie.” I have a gut feeling that’s what brought you here now. As Doomsday awakens dormant feelings about superheroes and multiverses, you probably need a guide to help you revisit all the best Marvel films or catch up on the ones you’ve missed. Lucky for you, it is easy to catch up. You just need time and a Disney+ subscription. If you start now, you’ll roll credits on The Fantastic Four: First Steps by December 17.

Here’s how to watch every Marvel movie before Avengers: Doomsday. Check back a year from now, when we’re doing it all over again for Avengers: Secret Wars.

Here’s the good news: Except for Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which came out this summer and is now on digital, every Marvel Cinematic Universe movie is available on Disney+. Every. Single. One.

Iron Man? Yes. Infinity War? Yup. Captain America: The Winter Soldier? Hell yeah. Guardians of the Galaxy? All three, baby! Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania? Maybe skip that one. And since Disney acquired Fox in 2018, you’ll also find all the X-Men, Deadpool, and the two Fantastic Four movies from the mid-2000s.

There’s also plenty of Marvel television. Not just streaming shows like WandaVision, The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, Ms. Marvel, and the recent VisionQuest, but also network shows like Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Agent Carter, as well as the Netflix Defenders-verse. If you’re really hardcore, you can also watch the handful of “One Shot” short films that were originally released on several Blu-rays.

The only “Marvel movies” you can’t watch on Disney+ are (most) of the Sony-produced movies. These include Morbius, Madame Web, Kraven the Hunter, and the Venom trilogy. But because distribution rights are funny, the Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield Spider-Man movies are on Disney+, along with Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse as I write this.

I hear you. Short of time-traveling back to 2000 and watching every movie as they come out, it feels impossible to “catch up” with all of it now. Especially since Avengers: Doomsday is once again dealing with the multiverse, which means even “non-canon” movies (like, say, the Blade or Punisher movies) might get a shout-out.

Luckily, Marvel knows your pain. On Disney+, a new “Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday” sub-page highlights the most important movies. While there are glaring omissions, watching only the highlighted movies can bump just about anyone up to speed. Even people who say they’ve “never seen one of these things.”

For your convenience, I’ve listed below EVERY movie from the Fox X-Men universe, the Sony Spider-Man universes, and the Marvel Cinematic Universe, in order of theatrical release. This is the only correct “viewing order.” Do not listen to YouTubers who insist on some “timeline order” nonsense. You can be an adult and watch these things exactly how they were produced and released. The movies Marvel deems essential for Doomsday prep are listed in bold, with the trailers attached.

Blade is rightfully credited with kickstarting the 21st-century superhero boom, but the X-Men films set the tone as must-see summer blockbusters. The first film in Fox’s X-Men series introduced audiences to mutants, with Hugh Jackman as Wolverine, the late Patrick Stewart as Charles Xavier, and Ian McKellen as radical extremist Magneto, who leads his Brotherhood in a fight for equal rights. Famke Janssen and James Marsden, who also starred as Jean Grey and Cyclops, respectively, will return in Doomsday, but Halle Berry’s Storm is sitting it out.

The battle for mutant liberation continues when Colonel Stryker (Brian Cox) kidnaps Xavier, forcing the X-Men to align with the Brotherhood of Mutants. In this better-than-you-remember sequel, mutantkind stands side by side for the sake of their survival. Though X2 predates shared universes, its scope, scale, and political intrigue make it one of the greatest and most underrated sequels of all time.

“I am Iron Man.” The resurrection of Robert Downey Jr.’s career blasted off to the stratosphere, along with the Marvel Cinematic Universe itself, in a movie that officially kicked off the MCU. Kidnapped by terrorists and forced into a cave with scraps, playboy futurist Tony Stark (Downey Jr.) escapes as the armored superhero Iron Man and returns home to find that his enemies are far closer to him than he suspects. When the smoke clears, a shadowy figure named Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson) informs him that the universe is way bigger than he knows.

Once, Chris Evans was the Human Torch. Suddenly, he wasn’t. As the Marvel Cinematic Universe picked up steam, the sweltering summer of 2011 saw Captain America: The First Avenger. Set in World War II, the first Marvel “prequel” stars Evans as the brave shrimp of Brooklyn, Steve Rogers, who becomes the first to endure the experimental “Super Soldier” program. As Captain America, Rogers takes the fight to Red Skull, whose dark ambition lies beyond the Third Reich.

There once was an idea: To bring together a remarkable group of cinematic superheroes to see if they can make cinematic history. In 2012, Marvel did just that. The first crossover Avengers movie saw the growing roster of Marvel’s cinematic superheroes team up for the very first time. Though Marvel movies have only gotten bigger and even better since, we cannot deny the seismic impact of The Avengers.

Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014)

After The Avengers planted the seeds for Thanos, all of Marvel’s storytelling shifted to an adaptation of the 1991 comic crossover The Infinity Gauntlet. In 2018, Marvel released Avengers: Infinity War, the third Avengers movie that forever changed the MCU’s status quo. With Josh Brolin as Thanos, the Marvel Universe’s many heroes band together to stave off the greatest threat anyone had ever seen. While audiences knew another movie was around the corner, its shock ending dared to ask the unthinkable: What happens when heroes lose?

It all came down to this. In 2019, on the same weekend Game of Thrones staged its own final battle, Avengers: Endgame changed the trajectory of the Marvel Universe once more. The fourth Avengers film sees the heroes dust off for a rematch against Thanos. But before they can do that, they must travel back in time through their own history to collect the Infinity Stones if they want to stand a chance.

In September 2026, in preparation for Doomsday, Marvel released an extended cut of Avengers: Endgame, titled Encore. It comes with a few extra minutes of scenes that frankly ruin the grace of Endgame in its original form, but if you really want to see clearer connective tissue to Doomsday, check out Encore.

In the 1970s, one of the most popular Marvel Comics titles wasn’t The Amazing Spider-Man, Uncanny X-Men, or The Avengers. It was Master of Kung Fu, starring an ass-kicker named Shang-Chi. He was a master martial artist and the son of a supervillain (Fu Manchu in the comics) who, over time, works as a secret agent for MI6. He was created by Steve Englehart and Jim Starlin (who also created Thanos) in the spirit of Bruce Lee and the TV show Kung Fu.

After decades of obscurity, the box-office success of Crazy Rich Asians in 2018 inspired Marvel to dig into the longboxes and put the spotlight back on Shang-Chi. In 2021, Simu Liu brought him to life in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, an origin movie that introduces Shang-Chi for the 21st century. Hong Kong screen legend Tony Leung (In the Mood for Love) costars as Wenwu, Shang-Chi’s father, who runs the terrorist group the Ten Rings—named after Wenwu’s mysterious alien weapons—which kidnapped Tony Stark in the first Iron Man.

Shang-Chi’s use of the Ten Rings has yet-unknown ties to the wider Marvel Universe. After five years, we may finally have some answers in Avengers: Doomsday.

After Spider-Man was publicly unmasked as Peter Parker at the end of Spider-Man: Far From Home, the teenage superhero turns to Sorcerer Supreme Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch) for help. But when the magic goes wrong, the multiverse cracks open, and villains from other realities—as in, other Spider-Man franchises—seep through the cracks. Tom Holland’s Spider-Man teams up with two veteran Spideys, played by Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield (remember them?), to put the universe back in one piece.

Doctor Strange saved the universe in Avengers: Endgame and restored the multiverse in Spider-Man: No Way Home. But can he save himself? In this direct sequel to 2016’s Doctor Strange and set after both Spider-Man: No Way Home and the Disney+ series WandaVision, Stephen must help protect a young girl, America Chavez (Xochitl Gomez), from a vengeful Wanda (Elizabeth Olsen), who wants to use America’s unique powers to reunite with her own lost family.

Originally billed as Marvel’s first horror movie (its very title alluding to Lovecraft’s At the Mountains of Madness), creative reshuffling led to Evil Dead and Spider-Man director Sam Raimi helming the movie. This explains the movie’s uniquely darker tone than one might expect from a typical Marvel tentpole. Cameos in this film tie directly to some of Marvel’s other far corners, like TV shows What If...? and Inhumans, as well as the Fox X-Men movies.

Werewolf by Night (2022), a “Marvel Studios Special Presentation” on Disney+

The real-life passing of Chadwick Boseman in 2020 left a huge hole in everyone’s hearts—and Marvel in a difficult place. Without its star, writer/director Ryan Coogler redesigned his plans for the sequel to his Earth-shattering 2018 hit.

Taking inspiration from Reginald Hudlin’s run in the comics, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever sets the stage for a new Black Panther: Shuri, T’Challa’s genius sister, played by Letitia Wright. But before Shuri can take up her brother’s mantle, she must first learn how heavy crowns are when another kingdom emerges from the depths and threatens Wakanda. The sequel introduces Namor (Tenoch Huerta), from the underwater world Talokan (originally Atlantis in the comics). The two will play a larger role in Avengers: Doomsday.

The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special (2022), a “Marvel Studios Special Presentation” on Disney+

After Hugh Jackman retired from playing Wolverine in the 2017 masterpiece Logan, Marvel and Ryan Reynolds shelled out a truckload of money to get him back and into some yellow spandex at last. The third movie in the Deadpool series, Deadpool & Wolverine, marked the MCU debut of Ryan Reynolds’ scrotum-faced Deadpool, whose dream of joining the Avengers clashes with the collapse of his own reality. More cameos, callbacks, and cusses fill the movie’s two-hour runtime.

While Jackman and Channing Tatum—who was once tapped to play the X-Men member Gambit, which Deadpool & Wolverine finally made a reality—will return in Doomsday, it’s unknown whether Reynolds will too. But if his surprise appearance at Comic-Con means anything, then...

When Steve Rogers gave Sam Wilson (Anthony Mackie) the shield of Captain America in Endgame, Sam wasn’t ready to take up the responsibility so soon. He still had his own things to work out. After the Disney+ series The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, Sam now flies the skies as Captain America, with the 2025 film Captain America: Brave New World marking the start of his era as the Star-Spangled Man. In addition to being the fourth Captain America movie, the movie revisits the events of 2008’s The Incredible Hulk and 2021’s Eternals.

The Marvel franchise was built on a studio elevating comic book benchwarmers into A-listers. That tradition was upheld in the 2025 movie Thunderbolts*. Based on a Marvel Comics series where supervillains form a team, the big-screen version recruits several “forgotten” antiheroes from different corners of the MCU. Together, they form a new team that must stave off their own assassination and save the world—on their terms. You can watch the movie cold, but know that many of these characters come from movies like Captain America: The Winter Soldier, Black Widow, Ant-Man and the Wasp, and the TV show The Falcon and the Winter Soldier.

And now, we step into a whole ‘nother world. After multiple attempts at a big-screen Fantastic Four, the Marvel Cinematic Universe launched its own take on the First Family in The Fantastic Four: First Steps. Set on a different Earth in 1964, the Fantastic Four rise to the occasion when the planet is threatened by Galactus.

Look. Don’t put yourself through that. There are too many. If you insist on watching any of them, just watch Loki. It has two seasons and just 12 episodes total, so you can knock it out in one weekend. Loki takes place after Avengers: Endgame (technically after just The Avengers, but how and why is too long to explain), and of all the shows, it bears the strongest ties to Doomsday. Talk about a glorious purpose.

#6794. Senate Democrats claim early wins in trio of key states

Former North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper, here at a campaign event in Rocky Mount, N.C., on Oct. 16, is the projected winner of the state's Senate race. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

Senate Democrats scored a few early wins in key races Tuesday night, according to The Associated Press, flipping the open seat in North Carolina and winning critical races in Georgia and New Hampshire.

Democrat Roy Cooper, the Tar Heel State’s battle-tested former governor who has never lost an election, extended his streak Tuesday by defeating Republican Michael Whatley. He becomes the first Democrat to win a Senate election in North Carolina since 2008.

In Georgia, Sen. Jon Ossoff, who started the midterm cycle as the most vulnerable Democratic senator, concluded it with a thrashing of his Republican opponent, Rep. Mike Collins.

And in New Hampshire, Rep. Chris Pappas will succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen after beating back a comeback attempt from Republican former Sen. John E. Sununu and denying Republicans one of their best pickup opportunities.

Democrats need a net gain of four seats to flip the Senate, and polls heading into Election Day showed the party competitive in several Senate races in traditionally Republican turf.

With his victory Tuesday, Ossoff heads into his second term with a growing national profile powered by clips of his searing critiques of President Donald Trump.

The Democrat raised an eye-popping $136.6 million through Oct. 14, swamping Collins, who brought in $10.7 million.

Georgia is a swing state that Trump carried by about 2 points in 2024. Four years earlier, Joe Biden had won the state by less than a quarter of a percentage point.

Before taking on Ossoff, Collins had to contend with a multicandidate primary, including fellow Rep. Earl L. “Buddy” Carter and former football coach and first-time candidate Derek Dooley.

Collins picked up Trump’s endorsement before the June primary runoff with Dooley, but a recent Atlanta Journal-Constitution/University of Georgia poll found the president with a 55 percent job disapproval rating.

Collins had been dogged by a House Ethics inquiry and reports that his son-in-law shared antisemitic and white nationalist social media posts.

Senate Republicans had initially hoped to persuade Brian Kemp, the state’s popular governor, to run for the seat, but he opted to endorse Dooley instead.

Cooper’s decisive win over Whatley, the former chair of the Republican National Committee, is a political blow to Trump, who was heavily invested in the contest.

The president publicly urged Whatley to run after Republican Sen. Thom Tillis, a sometimes critic, announced his retirement last year. Trump visited North Carolina twice since Labor Day, holding rallies in Gastonia and Greenville to boost Whatley. And Vice President JD Vance also campaigned for Whatley and other Republicans.

But Trump, who carried North Carolina in all three of his presidential races, has seen his approval fall sharply in the Tar Heel State: A poll released Sunday by the Center for Survey Research at East Carolina University found 54 percent of voters disapproving of the president’s performance.

At the start of the cycle, the North Carolina Senate race was thought to be among the nation’s most competitive. But on the eve of the election, Inside Elections with Nathan L. Gonzales rated the race Lean Democratic.

Senate Democrats had long been eager to recruit Cooper, who won four previous statewide elections for state attorney general and two as governor. He launched his campaign in July 2025, shortly after Tillis announced his retirement, and his fundraising prowess and deep roots in the state proved too much for Whatley, a first-time candidate, to overcome.

Cooper was also able to withstand GOP attacks that sought to paint him as a soft-on-crime ideologue who embraced a radical, far-left agenda and promoted “transgender ideology.”

Instead of diving into divisive culture war issues, Cooper hewed closely to an economic message, which was summed up by his campaign slogan: “Make Stuff Cost Less.” He portrayed Whately as a rubber-stamp for the unpopular president and a former energy company lobbyist who grew wealthy while rates rose.

The Trump administration “promised that cost of living would be the Day One issue,” Cooper said at a campaign stop in Rocky Mount last month. “Not only has that not been the case, they have made it so much worse.”

Pappas’ victory makes him the first openly gay man elected to the Senate, although he didn’t emphasize the potential milestone on the campaign trail.

A fourth-term House member, Pappas’ family owns a popular restaurant in the state that claims to have invented the chicken tender. He cast his campaign as crucial for Democrats to hold the Senate.

With his win, Pappas also dealt a loss to one of the state’s most prominent political families. Sununu’s father and brother previously served as New Hampshire governor.

Sununu, who conceded before 8:30 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday before the AP had called the race, was trying to win back a seat he held for a single term before losing to Shaheen in 2008.

The Granite State hasn’t elected a GOP senator since 2010, but Republicans, including Sununu’s brother, Chris, have been elected to the governor's mansion every two years since 2016.

#6791. A Guide to the Best Canada Goose Jackets

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

High performance or high fashion? There’s a pick for each.

Since 1957, Canada Goose has been crushing the luxury outerwear game. And if its decades of history tell you one thing, it’s that Canada Goose isn’t going anywhere anytime soon. In fact, one of the best decisions that you can make is investing in a piece or two (if you haven’t already) because it’s a purchase that’s going to pay off. The high-quality designs are durable, practical, and stand at a timeless intersection where fashion meets function.

The biggest issue we have with Canada Goose is that there are too many options to choose from. You’re probably already aware that the brand has more than just its hefty parkas. Sure, it’s got those too, of course, but we also love its bombers, flannels, and fleeces. Canada Goose brand has even been venturing into the high-fashion space, with its creative director Haider Ackermann debuting collaborations with the NBA’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, CNCPTS, and KidSuper, among others.To help you find the right fit for you, we did a full breakdown for you. Below, find our official guide to the six best Canada Goose jackets. You’re not going to regret getting any of these.

This bomber jacket has some history to it. Originally designed over 25 years ago, this iteration of the jacket fuses modern functionality with classic bomber detailing, like a double placket, pen pocket, and ribbed waist. The archive-inspired satin gives it a glossy finish, but it’s still subtle enough that it will go with pretty much just about anything. Wear it with some black jeans, combat or Chelsea boots, and you’ve got a badass fit.

Every man should own a bomber jacket, so if for some reason the Seguin Aviator didn’t resonate with you, maybe this one will. Inspired by the brand’s 2004 Air Force parka, this bomber adds a warm fleece for insulation—as well as style points. With five pockets (two welt pockets at the chest, two lower pockets with coin-snaps, one zippered sleeve pocket), it masters practicality.

You can never go wrong with a traditional puffer. It’s actually more of a prerequisite than anything else, especially if you live somewhere with an actual winter. Canada Goose’s puffer is top-of-the-line, as it’s ultra-lightweight, super soft, and durable. So many puffer jackets weigh you down, but this one doesn’t. Its features are also endless: There are backpack straps, recessed rib-knit cuffs that add comfort and lock in heat, interior drawcord to customize fit, two exterior fleece-lined handwarmer pockets with zipper closures, three interior pockets, two mesh drop-in pockets, one security pocket—and more.

If you want a streamlined parka that doesn’t have too much going on on the outside—but still has a ton of cool features inside—the Langford is the one for you. It has a sleek silhouette that’s slightly longer than a puffer, and it’s even warmer than a puffer, too. With 625 Fill Power down inside, it can protect you in temperatures down to -13°F, and it will look great while doing it. It also has an adjustable down-filled hood, lined chin guard, two-way zipper underneath snap closures, and fleece-lined upper hand pockets so you can really keep the cold out and turn up the warmth.

The Expedition Parka is Canada Goose’s original—and most iconic—extreme-weather jacket. Initially developed for scientists working in Antarctica, this jacket is made to keep you warm in the most extreme of environments. It does that—and then some—with its elasticized snow skirt for added protection, interior drawcord at the waist to customize fit and retain warmth, and double-entry pockets for easy access. We could elaborate even more here, but you can just check out our love letter to the iconic parka for all the details.

But this version is even cooler than the original: It’s part of the Snow Goose line, which is basically creative director Haider Ackermann’s passion project. It features some more fashion-forward designs, stuff that’s harder to wear. However, this version of the Expedition Parka keeps the classic shape, but it comes in two seasonal colors, so you’ll stand out from everyone else wearing the same model, but won’t feel like you’re on the runway. It’s a win-win.

We know this puffer jacket looks like a sweater, but that’s kind of the point: It has the fun design of a winter sweater and the warmth of a down jacket—and when you add in the soft feel of the exterior from the wool-alpaca blend, you’re getting a lot of good stuff. It doesn’t look too bulky, but it can keep you warm down to -4°F, if you can believe it. It’s a good alternative to the more classic polyester or nylon puffer jackets; just be careful about taking it out in heavy rain or snow, and keep in mind that the exterior material requires more delicate handling than the usual puffer jacket material.

#6788. The 63 Best New Perfumes and Fragrances of 2026

Every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

We sniffed, we spritzed, we sprayed. Only the perfumes below left a lingering impression, earning them a spot on our annual best-of list.

Everything smells like vanilla. At least, that’s what perfume naysayers will tell you. And it’s somewhat true: If you’re judging by what’s popular, ubiquitous, or cool with the youth, then sure—vanilla scents and sweet gourmands are still trending.

But hundreds of other fragrance launches in 2026 deserve a spot on your vanity and a spritz on your skin, and many are far less sweet. Gourmands took a turn for the weird and fruity this year, with notes like lychee and rice milk popping up in otherwise innocuous formulas. Woods and ambers continued to reign, as did spice-forward and citrus scents with unexpected depth. Perfumers are meeting our demand for newness in increasingly interesting, artistic ways, and we smelled hundreds of their creations to choose the 63 winners of our annual fragrance awards.

See all the winners of the 2026 Harper’s Bazaar Fragrance Awards, plus quotes from our beauty editors on what makes these formulas worthy of your next blind buy.

“Perfumer Olivier Polge reinvented the beloved “Coco Mad” scent as Crush Absolu, a new juice centered around patchouli, amber, rose, and a lychee-grapefruit accord. ‘There’s something voluptuous, something very prideful, something very addictive,’ Polge says about the new scent.”

“The new iteration of J’adore was inspired by Rihanna herself. As such, it’s a sweeter, bolder take, with notes of honeyed jasmine, rose, ylang-ylang, and vanilla.” —JR

"Bazaar’s Beauty Commerce Editor, Tiffany Dodson Davis, describes Guerlain’s L’Heure Bleue Eau de Parfum as the “scent of sunset,” thanks to a blue-sky accord that evokes the moment the sun goes down and the air turns crisp, clean, and fresh." —KI

Burberry Goddess Amber Vanilla Eau de Parfum Intense

“Lavender, maple syrup, four vanilla notes—I feel like a dog hearing all my favorite words. The result is a warm, ambery gourmand perfume that’s perfect for the cooler months.” —JR

Armani Emporio Armani Power of You Eau de Parfum

"Passionfruit adds an unexpected zing to the vanilla base here, making Power of You one of our favorite tropical-leaning gourmands of the year. It's pure summertime sex appeal." —JR

“Henry Rose Ripe captures fruits—from lychee to watermelon—at their juiciest, ripest point, like a delectable first bite, before packing a punch with black pepper, cardamom, and powdery florals.” —Katie Intner, beauty market and commerce editor

“One of the most unexpected fruity florals on the list, Influxious Magic Hour melds watermelon and dragon fruit with spicy chili pepper for a burst of juicy energy.” —KI

Balmain Paris Destin De Balmain Eau de Parfum

"The opening note of Destin is strawberry, a modern and sweet fruity note that quickly dries down to a patchouli-forward, gorgeous floral musk. It will make you smell expensive." —JR

"Neroli, bergamot, and yuzu combine with notes of orange blossom, jasmine, and tonka bean for a well-rounded fragrance that stands out from the pack. Parfum de Marly's Athénaïs eau de parfum has a zesty composition upon first spritz before drying down to a powdery finish." —Tiffany Dodson Davis, beauty commerce editor

“Gap recently brought back its iconic fragrance line from the ’90s, including the nostalgic Grass Eau de Parfum. It now features matcha, vetiver, green mandarin, and cedar for a fresh take on its outdoorsy, earthy scent.” —KI

“This stunning perfume is all gardenia and vanilla, and in its simplicity, it happens to be one of our most complimented scents of the year.” —JR

Maison Francis Kurkdjian Oud Velvet Mood Extrait de Parfum

"This is a bold, long-wearing scent for those who live and die for the sensual pairing of rose and oud. We're obsessed with the way it blooms and evolves on skin throughout the night." —JR

“Ex Nihilo Demon Dancer feels like moving through the crisp air on a spring day, with peppermint providing a breezy contrast to juicy rhubarb, bright bergamot, and warm tonka bean.” —KI

“We don’t know what we love more: the magnetic floral perfume that begs to be worn every day, the sculptural bottle, or the bookish packaging that made us a fan before we even took our first whiff.” —JR

“You can’t go wrong with Beyoncé’s sultry and sophisticated hair perfume, which leaves hair with a long-wearing trail of bergamot, jasmine, oud, sandalwood, and Haitian vetiver.” —JR

“Delightfully unisex, this aromatic scent is a masterclass in balance. The top opens with bergamot, cardamom, pink pepper, and wormwood. In the middle, you’ll find fruity fig, lavender, and violet leaf. The base is iris, amberwood, and ambrette.” —JR

“Earthy and green, with an olive top note and banana base note—this is the perfume to buy this year if you want to smell wholly original and unabashedly cool.” —JR

“Creamy and warm with notes of chocolate and coffee, this is the must-have gourmand perfume of the winter. In a word, it makes us feel happy.” —JR

Discothèque Next to Me or Nothing Eau De Parfum

“More of a feeling than a fragrance, this scent is airy and easy to wear, with breezy notes of milk, jasmine, and woods.” —JR

"Gourmand lovers will want to overindulge in this elevated eau de parfum, which combines two types of creams—whipped and coconut—along with jasmine blossom and vanilla mousse notes for a sophisticated yet playful olfactory blend." —TDD

“An olfactory version of a sound bath, Liis Forest Sounds boasts notes of bright yuzu, damp rain (earthier than plain water), green leaves, and woods.” —KI

Dolce&Gabbana Dolce&Gabbana Your Devotion Eau de Parfum Intense

"The notes in this fragrance sound good enough to eat: Sicilian lemon, orange blossom, and vanilla milk. This is a date-night, delicious gourmand for those who usually prefer a lighter citrus scent." —JR

Dries Van Noten Velvet Violet Eau de Parfum

“This woody-gourmand scent captures the lush texture of velvet with a mix of unusual notes: violet leaf, clary sage essence, toasted sesame, barley roasted, and grilled tonka beans.” —JR

Ellis Brooklyn Vanilla Rice Eau de Parfum

“Estée Lauder’s Glimmer gives crisp orange flower and rose a warm finish with vanilla bean, tonka bean, amber, and two types of wood.” —KI

“The latest addition to Glossier’s You fragrance lineup, Soie is an aquatic and solar take on a floral scent, with tropical Tiare flower water and creamy rice in place of powdery florals.” —KI

“Not quite a fragrance, Future Society’s Base Scent is like the no-makeup makeup version of perfume. Infused with prebiotics and a patent-pending technology, the scent is designed to enhance and balance any fragrance layered beneath it—whether that’s lotion, deodorant, or your natural scent—by working with the skin’s microbiome.” —KI

Harlem Perfume Co. Sensual Muse Eau de Parfum

“A fruity floral that reads as more sophisticated, Harlem Fragrance Co.’s Sensual Muse gives juicy apricot, bright citrus, and creamy gardenia a warm, compelling character once whipped vanilla, sandalwood, and amber are added into the mix.” —KI

“If you prefer your cocktails in fragrance form, look no further than By Kilian, which has mastered the art of turning a nutty, warm, slightly sweet espresso martini into a wearable scent that feels especially seductive at night.” —KI

#6786. Penélope Cruz Says It’s Time for Women Directors to Be the Norm

With Bunker, The Invite, and La Bola Negra all out this year, ELLE Women in Hollywood honoree Penélope Cruz told three very different stories through her characters. She dedicated her speech at our Women in Hollywood event to the writers and directors behind those projects, along with her The Invite co-star Seth Rogen. She also called out the lack of women directors in Hollywood, saying it’s time for things to change.

“I wanted to share this recognition with all the people that over the years have given me the opportunity to make a living out of this profession. That was my prayer every night,” Cruz began. “I also want to share it with four directors and two writers. Florian Zeller [who directed Bunker], thank you for your talent and for your trust and for allowing me to express through a character my anger and sadness about the fact that a story where people are building bunkers to save themselves is not a story of science fiction anymore. Thank you, Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrosi, my new best friends, for giving me the treasure of a character that is Nené Romero in your incredible, genius film, La Bola Negra. And Guitarrica is here, and so [I’m] sharing [this honor] with you and all the cast of the film.”

“I want to thank the incredible Olivia Wilde. You are brilliant,” she added of The Invite’s director. “I really loved making our film. The only thing that I didn’t like about it is that once again, when you are being directed by a woman, you get to do all the press, that is still the number one question: Does it feel very different to be directed by a woman? And I feel really like after 30 years working, when are we going to get to the day where that is not worth [it] to ask anymore because it’s just a normal, common thing? That is truly a very strong wish that I have.

“Seth [Rogen], I don’t know where you went, but what a privilege it has been to sing Sade for you in this film. What a privilege to work with you, with Edward [Norton], with Olivia, to be part of a film that brings people to the theater and makes them laugh and cry at the same time for two hours. People are stopping us in the streets now to tell us all their secrets about their relationships. And others, and I’m not joking, are sending us letters to inform us about their very recent divorce—in a good way. So, the process of making this movie was interesting. Everything had to happen very quickly, but thanks to the generosity of the writers Will [McCormack] and Rashida [Jones] and the generosity of Olivia, it happened. It was one of those miracles where everything gets put together very quickly, and it happened. And truly, it was important for me today to name Will and Rashida because I haven’t met in my career people with that amount of generosity and zero ego, so this is also for them.”

Cruz ended her speech by shouting out her longtime agent, team, and her brother, who attended the event with her.

Watch her full speech above and read her Women in Hollywood cover story here.

#6784. Tom Holland and Zendaya Wore a Couple of Fantastic Gold Watches to the Governors Awards

The timepieces themselves? Drastically different. The vibes? Entirely in sync.

Tom Holland and Zendaya were among the stars attending this past weekend’s Governors Awards in Los Angeles, where both made interesting choices when it came to their watches.

Holland, dressed in a black double-breasted Louis Vuitton dinner suit, white shirt, and black bow tie—with tan leather Christian Louboutin boots—was photographed pulling back his cuff to reveal a rose-gold Tank Louis Cartier on a leather strap.

Introduced in 1922, it's one of watchmaking's great enduring designs, with a list of famous admirers that includes Andy Warhol, Yves Saint Laurent, and Princess Diana.

Zendaya, meanwhile, went vintage. Her choice was a small, chic, solid-gold Rolex dating from the 1960s, believed to be the very watch she bought at a vintage market in her hometown of Oakland just over a week ago.

According to the San Francisco Chronicle, the actress spotted the watch at a stall run by independent dealer Wrist Glow Co., tried it on, went off to browse and returned an hour later to buy it. The price? A little over $6,000.

Watch-spotters have identified the Rolex as a ladies' cocktail watch, reference 8196, although that identification has yet to be independently confirmed.

So, what have we learned? Perhaps that for two stars who do old-school Hollywood glamour so well, there are few better choices for an awards-night watch than a classic in gold. Which one you go for, though, remains a matter of personal taste.
